evidence: push.py:630-638: `lead = ... ; payload = (...).encode('utf-8'); fd = os.open(exclude_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND); try: os.write(fd, payload) finally: os.close(fd)` — the changed code`
push.py:637-638: `except OSError: return False` — the write-failure handler

Test injects: `if args[:3] == ("rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/exclude"): return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 1, ...)` which hits push.py:619 `if resolved.returncode != 0 ... return False`, bypassing os.open/os.write entirely
ABSENCE: no test monkeypatches os.open/os.write or makes the exclude file unwritable to drive the except OSError branch that this diff rewrote
advisory.finding: The exclusion-WRITE failure path and its `except OSError` handler — the exact lines this diff introduces (os.open(O_APPEND)/os.write/os.close at push.py:632-638) — are not exercised by any test. test_exclusion_failure_splits_strict_from_default_and_retry injects the fault at `rev-parse --git-path info/exclude`, which returns False via the earlier `resolved.returncode != 0` branch (push.py:619) and never reaches the changed write code. A regression in the atomic-write sequence (e.g. an OSError from os.open/os.write escaping unclaught, a wrong open flag, or a leaked fd) would not be caught, despite the commit message claiming 'exclusion-write failure, strict and default' is pinned.
scenarios: A future edit forgets to wrap os.open/os.write in the try/except, letting OSError propagate uncaught out of commit_and_push_tickets_branch
A wrong open flag or fd-leak regression in the new atomic-write sequence
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a variant that monkeypatches push.os.open (or os.write) to raise OSError after rev-parse succeeds, then assert strict raises PushDeliveryError(reason='stage-failed') and default warns-and-returns None with the pending event retained — covering the actual changed write path rather than the resolve-failure branch.
